title: Brother James on preparing a place of rest
summary: Brother James and Mahalia discuss the Bible's ant proverb and providing for a place to stay.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: This is Brother James from Dayton, Ohio, wishing you all a very happy and prosperous summer. As we end into the fall season of the year, we trust that God's blessings will rain upon you. As you go into the winter months and the snows will fall upon the ground that you might provide for yourself a place of rest and place of worship.
Brother James, that was a very nice little speech that you made. I don't know why you thought of the idea of a place of rest.

Most people go into the winter months without providing for themselves a place to stay. They don't consider the Bible when it says go to the Ants out of the summer and consider ways to be wise and ants and doors up in the storehouses in the summer. They might have a place in the winter for rest.
You mean to say human beings don't think about a place of rest?
I wouldn't say human beings as a whole, but the majority don't. They enjoy summer while it's here and when it's over, then they start preparing for the winter.
Oh, I see. Well, I thought that was self-preservation for people to look out from one part of the year to the other.
I can't help but going back to the proverb about the Ants every time I think about self-preservation because they have it.

Yes. I know the Bible did explain about being as smart as the Ant. But that's the greatest thing in any human life is to look for a place to stay. A lot of people can't get anything else but a place to stay and something to eat. Just the things that they actually need.
